newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Uralmash to issue ADRs in Sept-Oct 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia Uralmash to issue ADRs in Sept-Oct 1997.

text.p: Russian heavy equipment maker AO Uralmash said on Tuesday holding company Uralmash Industries would place $30-$45 million in a new share issue in June or July this year, with level-one ADRs issued on the placement later.

"In June-July of this year, a new issue of 26.87 percent of the voting stock in Uralmash Industries shares will be placed on the international market," a statement released by AO Uralsky Zavod Tyazhelogo Mashinostroyeniya (Uralmash) said.

The statement said Uralmash Industries hoped to get $30-$45 million for modernisation of the plant from the placement and said Flemings and CentreInvest Securities had been chosen as lead managers for the share issue.
Dmitry Solomin, president of AO Finansovaya Kompaniya Neftyanoi Investitsionny Dom, which is coordinating the share issue for Uralmash, said the shares would be issued through a private placement.

He said that level-one American depositary receipts (ADRs), share look-alikes issued on extant shares and which can trade in the U.S., would be issued in the autumn on the share placement, to be exchanged for the shares on a voluntary basis.

"As soon as we know the results of the Uralmash Industries share placement a support programme will be started almost immediately in the form of an ADR programme," Solomin told a news conference on Tuesday.
"Realistically I think we can expect an ADR closer to autumn, in September or October."
He said the company's application to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission was currently being prepared.
Uralmash shares are currently not traded on the Russian Trading System.
Uralmash Industries has been set up as a holding company for AO Uralmash and ZSMK, another equipment maker which mostly produces for the larger company.

The statement said shares in Uralmash and ZSMK were already being swapped for shares in the new holding company and that Uralmash Industries currently holds 42 percent of voting shares in Uralmash and 30 percent in ZSMK.
Uralmash has cut personnel by 33 percent in recent years, decreased energy consumption by 30 percent since 1995 and is spinning off non-core units in a bid to restructure.

Foreign investors, who include New Century Holdings, Merrill Lynch, Chase Manhattan Bank, ING Baring, CS First Boston, Creditanstalt International and Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian), hold 20 percent of AO Uralmash.
Last month Russia sold 9.32 percent of the company for 41.44 trillion roubles, or 123,338 roubles per share, at an auction to Yekaterinburg's TOO Skela.
